arxiv-1804-11247.title: ReHabgame: A non-immersive virtual reality rehabilitation system with applications in neuroscience
arxiv-1804-11247.creator: Shabnam Sadeghi Esfahlani, Tommy Thompson, Ali Davod Parsa, Ian Brown, Silvia Cirstea
arxiv-1804-11247.description: Abstract This paper proposes the use of a non-immersive virtual reality rehabilitation system "ReHabgame" developed using Microsoft Kinect TM and the Thalmic TM Labs Myo gesture control armband. The ReHabgame was developed based on two third-person video games that provide a feasible possibility of assessing postural control and functional reach tests.

arxiv-2112-04868.title: RCSEDv2: homogenization of multi-wavelength photometric data.
arxiv-2112-04868.creator: Victoria Toptun, Igor Chilingarian, Ivan Katkov, Kirill Grishin, Anastasia Kasparova, Sviatoslav Borisov, Evgenii Rubtsov, Vladimir Goradzhanov, Vladislav Klochkov
arxiv-2112-04868.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Victoria Toptun, Igor Chilingarian, Ivan Katkov, Kirill Grishin, Anastasia Kasparova, Sviatoslav Borisov, Evgenii Rubtsov, Vladimir Goradzhanov, Vladislav Klochkov. RCSEDv2 (https://rcsed2.voxastro.org/), the second Reference Catalog of Spectral Energy Distributions of galaxies includes the largest homogeneously processed photometric dataset for 4 million galaxies assembled from several wide-field surveys. Here we describe the methodology of the photometric data homogenization.

arxiv-2308-16644.title: Paired kernels and their applications
arxiv-2308-16644.creator: M. Cristina Câmara, Jonathan R. Partington
arxiv-2308-16644.description: Abstract This paper considers paired operators in the context of the Lebesgue Hilbert space on the unit circle and its subspace, the Hardy space H 2 H^{2} . The kernels of such operators, together with their analytic projections, which are generalizations of Toeplitz kernels, are studied. Results on near-invariance properties, representations, and inclusion relations for these kernels are obtained.

arxiv-2405-18781.title: On the Role of Attention Masks and LayerNorm in Transformers
arxiv-2405-18781.creator: Xinyi Wu, Amir Ajorlou, Yifei Wang, Stefanie Jegelka, Ali Jadbabaie
arxiv-2405-18781.description: Abstract Self-attention is the key mechanism of transformers, which are the essential building blocks of modern foundation models. Recent studies have shown that pure self-attention suffers from an increasing degree of rank collapse as depth increases, limiting model expressivity and further utilization of model depth.

arxiv-2412-06287.title: PediaBench: A Comprehensive Chinese Pediatric Dataset for Benchmarking Large Language Models
arxiv-2412-06287.creator: Qian Zhang, Panfeng Chen, Jiali Li, Linkun Feng, Shuyu Liu, Heng Zhao, Mei Chen, Hui Li, Yanhao Wang
arxiv-2412-06287.description: Abstract The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the medical domain has stressed a compelling need for standard datasets to evaluate their question-answering (QA) performance. Although there have been several benchmark datasets for medical QA, they either cover common knowledge across different departments or are specific to another department rather than pediatrics.

arxiv-2510-23102.title: Exotic B-series representation of the Feller semigroup for Itô diffusions and the MSR path integral
arxiv-2510-23102.creator: A. Bonicelli
arxiv-2510-23102.description: Abstract In this paper we consider the expansion of the Feller semigroup of a one-dimensional Itô diffusion as a power series in time. Taking our moves from previous results on expansions labelled by exotic trees, we derive an explicit expression for the combinatorial factors involved, that leads to an exotic Butcher series representation.

arxiv-2510-24796.title: Mutual Wanting in Human–AI Interaction: Empirical Evidence from Large-Scale Analysis of GPT Model Transitions Thanks: Complete development history and code: https://github.com/assassin808/Mutual-Wanting
arxiv-2510-24796.creator: GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, HaoYang Shang, Xuan Liu
arxiv-2510-24796.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, HaoYang Shang, Xuan Liu. The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) creates complex bidirectional expectations between users and AI systems that are poorly understood. We introduce the concept of "mutual wanting" to analyze these expectations during major model transitions. Through analysis of user comments from major AI forums and controlled experiments across multiple OpenAI models, we provide the first large-scale empirical validation of bidirectional desire dynamics in human-AI interaction.

arxiv-2601-00197.title: StockBot 2.0: Vanilla LSTMs Outperform Transformer-based Forecasting for Stock Prices Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2601-00197.creator: Shaswat Mohanty
arxiv-2601-00197.description: Abstract Accurate forecasting of financial markets remains a long-standing challenge due to complex temporal and often latent dependencies, non-linear dynamics, and high volatility. Building on our earlier recurrent neural network framework, we present an enhanced StockBot architecture that systematically evaluates modern attention-based, convolutional, and recurrent time-series forecasting models within a unified experimental setting.

pmc-10533106.title: Revascularization and Left Ventricular Dysfunction for ICD Eligibility
pmc-10533106.creator: Letizia Rosa Romano, Carmen Anna Maria Spaccarotella, Ciro Indolfi, Antonio Curcio, Aleksei N Sumin, Dmitry V Duplyakov, Alexey N Repin
pmc-10533106.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Common triggers for sudden cardiac death (SCD) are transient ischemia, hemodynamic fluctuations, neurocardiovascular influences, and environmental factors. SCD occurs rapidly when sinus rhythm degenerates into ventricular tachycardia (VT) and/or ventricular fibrillation (VF), followed by asystole. Such progressive worsening of the cardiac rhythm is in most cases observed in the setting of ischemic heart disease and often associated with advanced left ventricular (LV) impairment. Revascularization prevents negative outcomes including SCD and heart failure (HF) due to LV dysfunction (LVD).

pmc-10615918.title: Benzophenone-3 does not Cause Oxidative Stress or B-esterase Inhibition During Embryo Development of Octopus maya (Voss and Solís Ramírez, 1966)
pmc-10615918.creator: Gissela Moreno-Ortiz, Letícia Aguilar, Claudia Caamal-Monsreal, Elsa Noreña-Barroso, Carlos Rosas, Gabriela Rodríguez-Fuentes
pmc-10615918.description: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is an active ingredient in sunscreen lotions and personal-care products that protects against the damaging effects of ultraviolet rays. Given its worldwide dissemination, it has been linked with harmful effects on aquatic biota; however, its impact is not fully understood calling for further studies.

pmc-10679725.title: Short-chain fatty acids are potential goalkeepers of atherosclerosis
pmc-10679725.creator: Yu Feng, Danyan Xu
pmc-10679725.description: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are metabolites produced by gut bacteria and play a crucial role in various inflammatory diseases. Increasing evidence suggests that SCFAs can improve the occurrence and progression of atherosclerosis. However, the molecular mechanisms through which SCFAs regulate the development of atherosclerosis have not been fully elucidated.

pmc-10735735.title: MULTILEVEL LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS ARE NEEDED TO IMPROVE DIABETES SELF-MANAGEMENT IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10735735.creator: Yan Du, Lixin Song, Mitzi Gonzales, Sara Espinoza, Carlos Jaen, Bei Wu, Erin Finley
pmc-10735735.description: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a major public health concern in older adults. Physical activity (PA) and healthy eating (HE) are two major lifestyle intervention strategies in diabetes self-management for controlling glucose levels, preventing complications, and improving functionality and quality of life.

pmc-11437157.title: Structural design and experimental verification of a thin-walled plastic chairs based on the finite element method
pmc-11437157.creator: Ling Song, Minggong Yu, Delin Sun
pmc-11437157.description: This study focuses on the design and preparation of a thin-walled plastic chair, and its mechanical properties were investigated by high load, cyclic load and drop impact. The finite element method (FEM) was employed to accurately evaluate the chair’s safety under these forces. Additionally, the effects of important structural parameters on the loading process in different states were investigated.

pmc-11543979.title: Present and Future of Pharmacological Management for Acute Moderate-to-Severe Postoperative, Traumatic, or Musculoskeletal Pain in Europe: A Narrative Review
pmc-11543979.creator: Eugene R Viscusi, Francisco Epelde, Luis Javier Roca Ruiz, Eva Trillo-Calvo
pmc-11543979.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Acute moderate-to-severe pain is common after surgery, trauma, or musculoskeletal injury, but its management remains suboptimal. Current single-agent treatments are limited by safety concerns, narrow therapeutic windows, and abuse potential, leaving substantial unmet needs. Here, we aimed to review guidelines for the management of acute moderate-to-severe post-surgical, trauma-related, or musculoskeletal pain in adults and discuss existing and potential future analgesics in this setting. We searched PubMed to identify relevant guidelines and existing analgesics for acute pain.
